units: Keth. 48ᵃ שארה זו ק׳ בשר וכ׳ her sh’er (Ex. XXI, 10), this means the immediate contact of bodies, that he must not treat her in the manner of the Persians &c.
<cite ref="Shabbat 13b:1">Sabb. 13ᵇ</cite> <he>ישן עמי בק׳ בשר</he> he slept by my side (under one cover) undressed; Y. Kidd. IV, 66ᶜ <he>וישן עמהן בק׳ בשר</he> and he may sleep with them &c.—

<cite ref="Bava Batra 7b:13">B. Bath. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>לפי ק׳ בתים הן גובין</he> fortification taxes are raised in proportion to the propinquity of the houses to the city wall. Y. Maas. Sh. I, end, 53ᵃ (ref. to <cite ref="Deuteronomy 14:24">Deut. XIV, 24</cite>) <he>בק׳ מקום</he> when the place is near Jerusalem, opp. <he>בריחוק</he>.—
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kiddushin 4:1:5">Y. Kidd. IV, beg. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>ק׳ פנים</he> bringing the face near, i.e. welcome reception (of proselytes).

Sot. 49ᵃ; Yalk. Hab. 563 (ref. to Hab. III, 2) א״ת בקרב שנים בק׳ שְׁנַיִם read not b’ḳereb shanim (in the midst of years), but b’ḳerub sh’nayim, in the contact of two (poor scholars wrapped in one cloak); a. e.
